It has its own ROHM sheet bu97960muv-e.pdf (34 pages; https://fscdn.rohm.com/en/products/databook/datasheet/ic/driver/lcd_segment/bu97960muv-e.pdf answers with a PDF; a copy is in scratchpad/g2/lsi/bu97960muv-e.pdf, not filed in datasheets/): 1/8 or 1/4 duty, COM0-COM7 with COM4-COM7 shared with SEG18-SEG15, 15 x 8 bit DDRAM, EVR contrast register, VQFN028V5050. Eight backplanes are beyond the lcd driver (static to 1:4), so it cannot be modeled; file the sheet and decide whether a 1:4-only partial model is wanted.

engineNeeds.need: multiplex mode chosen by a register field (PCF8553, PCA8553 MUX)
engineNeeds.keys: display.mode as an object {"field": "DISP1.MUX", "values": {"0": "1:4", "1": "1:3", "2": "1:2", "3": "static"}}; display.backplanes keeps the four names; with n backplanes active the frame has n slots (slot = frame / n) and the unused backplane pins are released; the RAM bit (segment, backplane) layout does not change with the mode (ramOrder backplane, 5 bytes per backplane), so only the slot count and the released pins change
engineNeeds.why: pcf8553 p.8 Table 6: MUX[1:0] 00 1:4, 01 1:3, 10 1:2, 11 static. Today the device is fixed to a four-backplane frame; the register is stored. A glass of fewer backplanes wired to COM0.. shows the right cells (bench: 8D-1:3, 4D-1:2 and 4D-STATIC), only the pin waveform differs from the silicon. The ROHM chips are fixed 1/4 duty and need nothing.

engineNeeds.need: frame time chosen by a register field
engineNeeds.why: pcf8553 p.7 Table 5, bu91795 p.12, bu9796axxx-e p.13; the frame time is fixed at the reset value today (64 Hz, 80 Hz).

engineNeeds.keys: display.blink {"field": "DISP2.BL", "periodsUs": {"1": 2000000, "2": 1000000, "3": 500000}} (and BLKCTL.B for the ROHM chips): while the field is nonzero the display alternates between shown and off (every pin released) each half period
engineNeeds.why: pcf8553 p.8-9 Table 7 and 7.2.3.1 ('During the blank-out phase of the blinking period, the display is turned off'), bu91795 p.13; the duty of the blank phase is not given by either sheet. Stored only today.

engineNeeds.need: all pixels on regardless of the RAM (ROHM APCTL P1)
engineNeeds.keys: display.allOn: a condition (here APCTL.APON=1); while it holds every RAM bit reads 1 (each segment pin carries the inverse of the active backplane), the RAM is unchanged; the existing enable / APOFF condition wins
engineNeeds.why: bu91795 p.13, bu9796axxx-e p.15: all pixels on regardless of DDRAM, DDRAM unchanged, valid in display-on state; P0 (all off) wins when both are set. APOFF is modeled through the enable condition; APON is stored only.

engineNeeds.keys: display.disabledLevel 0 (or "low"): while the enable condition is false every backplane and segment pin is driven 0 instead of released
engineNeeds.why: pcf8553 p.10 (power-down: all outputs set to VSS), bu91795 p.13 and p.20 (segment and common ports output VSS after one frame of off data). A glass reads both the same; a probe on the pin does not.

engineNeeds.need: a pointer action that keeps the current address, and pointer wrap-around
engineNeeds.keys: protocol command action "pointer" without an address (or "address": "keep") that starts the auto-increment payload at the current pointer; a pointer "wrap": true that goes from the last register of a space back to its first
engineNeeds.why: ROHM chips: a command byte with C = 0 is followed by RAM data that is written at the current DDRAM address (bu91795 p.9: after an ADSET, the address is kept; p.9 / bu9796axxx-e p.10: after 13h the address returns to 00h). Modeled: C = 0 on ADSET and on the ICSET reset (address 00h) write RAM; C = 0 on every other command sends the data to a sink register (dropped); the address stays on the last register instead of wrapping.

engineNeeds.need: an I2C strap pin left open reads as 0
engineNeeds.keys: bus.i2c.table index digit for an open pin (a fifth tie value, or a bus key "openAs": 0)
engineNeeds.why: pcf8553 p.39 15.3: A0, A1, PORE and IFS have internal latching pull-downs, 'connect to VSS (or leave open) for logic 0'. Today only a pin tied to VSS or VDD gives an address; A0 / A1 left open (Z) answer nothing (bench: removed, noted in the spec).

engineNeeds.need: an oscillator output and an external clock input (CLK pin, OSC and COE bits)
engineNeeds.keys: none proposed; nothing in the sheets a host can observe except the clock itself
engineNeeds.why: pcf8553 p.7: OSC = 1 needs an external clock on CLK ('removing the clock may freeze the LCD in a DC state'), COE = 1 puts the clock on CLK. Stored only; the display runs whatever OSC says.

notes: Five lcddriver devices: PCF8553 and PCA8553 (40 x 4, `i2c-spi` bus: I2C 0x38-0x3B by A0 / A1 and 3-wire SPI by IFS, registers 00h-03h plus a 20-byte RAM, Software_reset 2Ch, RST pin, DE display enable; the two differ only in the width of Device_ctrl FF), BU91795 (VQFN24, 12 x 4), BU9796AFS (SSOP-A32, 20 x 4) and BU9796AMUV (VQFN24, 12 x 4): I2C write-only at 0x3E, the C-bit command chain (ICSET, DISCTL, ADSET, MODESET, BLKCTL, APCTL, each in a C = 1 and a C = 0 form), 4-bit DDRAM with auto-increment, display on/off, all-pixel-off, software reset. Eight parts: PCF8553DTT/AJ (obsolete), /AY, PCA8553DTT/AJ (obsolete, automotive), /AY (automotive), BU91795MUF-ME2 (automotive), BU9796AFS-E2, BU9796AMUV-E2, BU9796AMUV-ZE2. Footprints: TSSOP-56 reused; three new (VQFN-24-4X4-ROHM, VQFN-24-4X4-ROHM-A, SSOP-A32-ROHM, the last with the foot length taken as the whole 1.2 mm lead projection because the drawing does not print it). Four datasheet entries. Validated in a private copy (built Release): library_check passes; listing_check, trace_check and footprint_check differ from the goldens only by the added lines (8 parts, 3 footprints; trace_check 'lcd 7' is the existing kind row); lcd_spi_i2c_test passes (it needs `logic_test(lcd_spi_i2c_test)` in backend/CMakeLists.txt). The bench reads internal registers through SimComponentType.registers. BU97960MUV-E2 is skipped (own datasheet, eight backplanes). Cells of the glass are checked against the RAM for 1:4 (GENERIC-LCD-8D-1:4), 1:3, 1:2 and static glass; the multiplex mode is not switched by MUX (engineNeeds).
